about: Hand-written story cases for scripts/measure_misses.py: a first chapter that establishes something, a neutral chapter, and a last chapter that contradicts it (expect = the words where it goes wrong) or doesn't (expect = null).

chapters: Mara had never learned to swim, and the sea frightened her. She kept to the middle of the quay when she walked to the chandler's, well away from the edge, and she would not set foot in her uncle's boat even when it was tied up.

The market filled slowly that morning. Carts came down from the hill farms with cabbages and late apples, and the fishwives set their baskets along the wall. A boy chased a goose between the stalls until the baker caught it by the neck and handed it back to its owner. By noon the square smelled of bread and brine, and nobody spoke of anything but the price of salt.
The buoy had slipped its chain. Mara dived off the quay and swam hard for the far buoy, hauled it back against the tide and climbed the ladder laughing, water streaming from her hair.
cases.expect: Mara dived off the quay and swam hard

chapters: The fall from the loft broke Jonas's left arm in two places. The bonesetter bound it in splints and told him he would not lift so much as a spoon with it before midsummer.

The market filled slowly that morning. Carts came down from the hill farms with cabbages and late apples, and the fishwives set their baskets along the wall. A boy chased a goose between the stalls until the baker caught it by the neck and handed it back to its owner. By noon the square smelled of bread and brine, and nobody spoke of anything but the price of salt.
Next morning Jonas was in the yard before light. He swung the axe with both hands and split the whole cord of oak before breakfast, whistling as he worked.

chapters: They had sold the grey mare at the autumn fair to pay the rent. Ilse cried when the dealer led her away, and the stable stood empty all winter.

chapters: Anselm was an only child. His mother said so often, with a sigh, that one had been quite enough, and he had grown up alone in the big house.

By noon the square smelled of bread and brine, and nobody spoke of anything but the price of salt.
Anselm wrote that night to his brother in the city, as he had every week since they were boys, and asked him for the loan of forty crowns.
